title: Complementary Roles of Small Extracellular Vesicles and Matrix-Bound Vesicles in Tissue Regeneration Revealed by Proteomic Analysis
content: Mesenchymal stromal cell (MSC)-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) are promising mediators of tissue regeneration, yet the molecular differences between small EVs (sEVs) and matrix-bound vesicles (MBVs) remain insufficiently understood. We compared sEVs and MBVs derived from MSCs of four tissue sources: umbilical cord, adipose tissue, gingiva, and dental pulp, using LC–MS/MS proteomics and functional enrichment analysis. A total of 6,657 proteins were identified, including 3,644 (54.7%) shared between both vesicle populations, 999 (15.0%) detected only in MBVs, and 2,014 (30.3%) only in sEVs. Principal component analysis and hierarchical clustering revealed that vesicle type was the major factor associated with proteomic variability, whereas differences related to MSC tissue origin and individual donors were less pronounced. sEVs were enriched in proteins associated with extracellular matrix organization, angiogenesis, and cell migration, whereas MBVs showed enrichment of immune-regulatory, mitochondrial, and integrin-associated proteins. In macrophages, both vesicle populations reduced the expression of glycolysis-associated genes, while MBVs additionally increased PPARG, PPARGC1B, TFAM, and IL10 expression. These findings suggest that sEVs and MBVs possess distinct molecular signatures and may contribute to complementary aspects of tissue regeneration.
